templates.name: code-review
templates.summary: Reviews a pull request against your CODEREVIEW.md with eight independent reviewers. Every finding quotes its line.

templates.name: inbound-lead
templates.summary: Researches each new lead, scores it against your ideal customer profile and posts the brief to your CRM or Slack.

templates.name: kyb
templates.summary: Checks who owns and runs a company, screens it against the sanctions lists and gives a cited verdict.

templates.name: market-monitor
templates.summary: Every Monday, a short digest of what changed at the companies you watch, each item dated and linked.

templates.name: release-notes
templates.summary: Turns the pull requests merged since your last release into draft release notes for a person to edit.

templates.name: battlecard
templates.summary: A sourced battlecard on one competitor that a seller can use in a deal.

templates.name: company-brief
templates.summary: A sourced, dated brief on one company before a sales call, renewal or investment.

templates.name: deal-flow
templates.summary: Every Monday, the funding rounds, acquisitions and exits in one sector, each linked to its source.

templates.name: deal-hygiene
templates.summary: Once a week, posts the open HubSpot deals that went quiet, have no next step or are past their close date.

templates.name: dependency-health
templates.summary: A dated health check on one package before you adopt it, from its registry, repository and advisories.

templates.name: earnings-brief
templates.summary: What each ticker you watch reported since the last run, set against a named consensus.

templates.name: failed-payments
templates.summary: Posts a Slack alert for each failed Stripe payment with who, how much, why and the next step.

templates.name: hiring-signals
templates.summary: Every Monday, the new roles and leadership moves at the companies you track, and what they suggest.

templates.name: issue-triage
templates.summary: Labels each new GitHub issue, links likely duplicates and asks the author for what's missing.

templates.name: linear-sprint-check
templates.summary: Twice a week, posts which issues in your Linear cycle are slipping and what was added since it started.

templates.name: linear-triage
templates.summary: Labels each new Linear issue, links likely duplicates and asks for what's missing.

templates.name: literature-review
templates.summary: A cited review of the open research on one question. It opens every paper it cites and checks for retractions.

templates.name: market-sizing
templates.summary: Sizes a market top-down and bottom-up, with every number sourced or marked as an assumption.

templates.name: meeting-prep
templates.summary: A one-page brief on the person you're meeting and their organization, from public sources.

templates.name: oss-tracker
templates.summary: A weekly health check of the open-source projects you depend on or compete with.

templates.name: pipeline-goal
templates.summary: Posts in Slack the first time your open HubSpot pipeline passes the goal you set.

templates.name: release-shipped
templates.summary: Posts a short note to Slack when you publish a GitHub release, and thanks the people who built it.
templates.setup: Public repositories only: it watches the repository's release feed, and a private repository's feed needs a login. Make one fine-grained GitHub token with Contents read-only on that repository, and add it as the GitHub (token) server in Settings → MCP servers with Read-only on.

templates.name: revenue-goal
templates.summary: Posts in Slack the first time this period's Stripe revenue passes your goal.

templates.name: search-visibility
templates.summary: Every Monday, where your domain ranks for the queries you track and what moved since last week.

templates.name: stale-pr-digest
templates.summary: Once a week, posts the pull requests in one repository that have waited too long, and on whom.

templates.name: tender-finder
templates.summary: Every Monday, the open public tenders that match what you sell, each checked on the buyer's own notice.

templates.name: user-voice
templates.summary: Every Monday, the themes users raise about your product in reviews and forums, with linked quotes.

templates.name: vendor-outage-watch
templates.summary: A weekly brief on the outages at the vendors you depend on, read from their own status pages.
templates.setup: Optional: list your vendors' status feeds (a Statuspage page's is https://<status host>/history.atom) and it also alerts on each new incident and each change of its status, checking every 15 minutes. Leave the list empty and it is the weekly brief alone.

templates.name: vulnerability-digest
templates.summary: Every morning, the new CVEs and security releases that hit the software you list, and what to do about each.

templates.name: website-change-tracker
templates.summary: Watches the pages you name and reports the changes that matter, with the old and new text.

templates.name: morning-brief
templates.summary: Each weekday morning, one plan for your day in Slack, built from your calendar, mail and channels.

templates.name: calendar-brief
templates.summary: Your next few days of meetings in Slack each morning, with the clashes and what to prepare.

templates.name: team-catch-up
templates.summary: A short Slack post on the decisions, unanswered requests and blockers in your team's channels.

templates.name: follow-up-drafter
templates.summary: Writes your next reply as a Gmail draft when an email lands in a label you pick.

templates.name: meeting-follow-up
templates.summary: Saves a follow-up email draft for each outside meeting that ended today.

templates.name: support-inbox-digest
templates.summary: Once a week, posts the themes in your support mail to Slack, ranked by how many threads raised them.

templates.name: outreach-opener
templates.summary: Researches a person and their company, then saves a short first email to them as a Gmail draft.

templates.name: platform-changes
templates.summary: A weekly list of breaking changes, deprecations and price changes in the platforms you build on.

templates.name: terms-change-watch
templates.summary: Sends a clause-by-clause redline when a vendor changes its terms or privacy policy.

templates.name: enforcement-digest
templates.summary: A weekly digest of the fines and enforcement actions your regulators took against firms like yours.

templates.name: brand-mentions
templates.summary: A daily list of new public mentions of your company, and which ones need an answer.

templates.name: regulatory-tracker
templates.summary: A weekly brief on new and proposed rules in the area of law you track, with their key dates.

templates.name: sanctions-update
templates.summary: A weekly update on sanctions list changes, checked against the names you hold.

templates.name: product-recall-watch
templates.summary: A weekly check of recalls and safety notices for the products and makers you care about.

templates.name: competitor-content
templates.summary: Every Monday, what your competitors published that week and the topics nobody covered.

templates.name: content-ideas
templates.summary: Every Monday, four or five content ideas, each tied to something that happened that week.

templates.name: job-watch
templates.summary: Every weekday morning, the new job postings that match your role, location and must-haves.

templates.name: research-field-weekly
templates.summary: Every Monday, the week's notable papers, datasets and deadlines in one research field.

templates.name: supplier-discovery
templates.summary: Describe what you need to buy and get a ranked shortlist of manufacturers that make it.

templates.name: buyer-evidence
templates.summary: Public proof for each objection a skeptical buyer may raise, every row dated and linked.

templates.name: grant-finder
templates.summary: Finds the grants, fellowships and open calls you can still apply to, ranked by fit and deadline.

templates.name: seo-audit
templates.summary: Checks your site and up to five keywords, then hands back a ranked list of fixes.

templates.name: lead-list-builder
templates.summary: A list of companies that match your ideal customer, with up to two people at each.

templates.name: market-entry
templates.summary: Whether to enter one new country or segment, with a go, conditional go or no-go call.

templates.name: investment-memo
templates.summary: A cited first-draft investment memo on one company, for you to edit before committee.

templates.name: industry-primer
templates.summary: A sourced primer on one industry in one region, enough to talk about it tomorrow.

templates.name: industry-events
templates.summary: A dated calendar of the conferences and deadlines in your industry that are worth your time.

templates.name: audience-research
templates.summary: Who buys what you sell, what they struggle with and where to reach them, each point cited.

templates.name: country-risk
templates.summary: A sourced risk profile of one country before you pay, onboard or operate there.

templates.name: product-teardown
templates.summary: A teardown of one product from its public pages, docs and reviews.

templates.name: positioning-review
templates.summary: How your positioning holds up against named competitors, with sharper options to try.

templates.name: inbox-assistant
templates.summary: Sorts each new email, drafts your replies to the ones that need you, and leaves you a digest every evening.
templates.setup: Before you install, connect your mailbox under Settings → Email with an app password. Gmail, Fastmail and iCloud work, and so does any other mail provider. It runs on your machine and on your ChatGPT plan.

templates.name: pr-alert
templates.summary: Tells you about each new pull request on a public GitHub repo: who sent it, what it touches and what to watch.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed, and no GitHub token. It reads the repo's open pull requests every 30 minutes and sends one alert per new PR, on the free Ling 3.2 Flash model. GitHub is read anonymously, so point it only at a public repository.

templates.name: web-researcher
templates.summary: Answers one question from the open web: a short answer, each finding with its link, and where sources disagree.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed. Search is Exa's keyless tier, about 150 searches a day. Add the Parallel Search server (Settings → MCP servers, its preset) and search keeps working when that free tier runs out. Parallel sees each query, so ask only public questions.

templates.name: upgrade-watch
templates.summary: Every Monday, says whether upgrading a project you depend on is safe for what you use from it, each break quoted from its release notes.

templates.name: review-pulse
templates.summary: Every Monday, G2, Capterra and Trustpilot reviews of you and up to three rivals, in themes with quotes. Uses monid, billed per call.

templates.name: funding-radar
templates.summary: Every Monday, the new funding rounds in your sectors: amount, who led, what the company does, with links. Uses monid, billed per round.

templates.name: insider-moves
templates.summary: Every Monday, insider buys and sells on your watchlist, big buys flagged, each with its SEC filing. Not investment advice. Uses monid.

templates.name: reading-list
templates.summary: Every week, the top posts from your RSS and Atom feeds for what you care about, each with a two-line why and its link, never repeating an earlier week.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed. It reads only your feeds, so it needs no search provider. Set the feeds, your interests and the schedule when you apply it.

templates.name: field-monitor
templates.summary: A weekly report on what changed in one topic, each change dated and cited to the page that says it, with what it could not check.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed. Search is Exa's keyless tier, about 150 searches a day. Add Firecrawl's keyless server (Settings → MCP servers, the Firecrawl preset) and it keeps searching when that runs out and reads pages drawn by JavaScript. Firecrawl sees each query and URL, so use it for public pages only.

templates.name: page-to-json
templates.summary: Give it a URL and a JSON Schema and it returns typed JSON from that page, each value with the text it came from and each missing one null with a reason.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed. It reads the one page you give it. Add Firecrawl's keyless server (Settings → MCP servers, the Firecrawl preset) to read pages drawn by JavaScript. Firecrawl sees each query and URL, so use it for public pages only.

templates.name: ai-search-visibility
templates.summary: Checks whether ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google's AI crawlers can reach your site, whether you have an llms.txt and whether buyer searches find you, then lists what to fix first.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed. Search is Exa's keyless tier, about 150 searches a day. Add Firecrawl's keyless server (Settings → MCP servers, the Firecrawl preset) and it keeps searching when that runs out. Firecrawl sees each query and URL, so use it for public pages only.

templates.name: docs-answerer
templates.summary: Answers a question from one product's own docs site only, each point linked to the page that says it, and says plainly when the docs don't cover it.
templates.setup: Put an OPENROUTER_API_KEY in your server's environment; no credits are needed. Search is Exa's keyless tier, about 150 searches a day. Add Firecrawl's keyless server (Settings → MCP servers, the Firecrawl preset) and it keeps searching the docs site when that runs out. Firecrawl sees each query and URL, so use it for public pages only.
